The grep that said covered

PR playground for #4038: every release PR was red until a bot rescued it, twice, for the same reason as last time.

Why nobody found it by searching

The config does contain .codex-plugin/plugin.json. Search for it and you get a hit:

"path": "src/codex/ork-codex/.codex-plugin/plugin.json"     stamped
       ^^^ the SOURCE

"path": "plugins/ork-codex/.codex-plugin/plugin.json"      MISSING
"path": "plugins/ork/.cursor-plugin/plugin.json"           MISSING

A substring match returns a result and reads as covered. The mirror it actually needed was never there, and the Cursor one had no entry under any reading.

The loop

release-please bumps the SOURCE
        ↓
npm run build regenerates the MIRRORS from it
        ↓
mirrors sit inside ci.yml's build-drift roster
        ↓
release-please does not run a build
        ↓
Build check RED on every release PR
        ↓
autoheal bot pushes a second commit  →  green

The bot is why this survived. The end state is green, so nobody reads the intermediate red. beta.13 needed 9cc19029; beta.14 needed 50b86d3b then 430b1ca0.

Second recurrence, not first

The two Codex source manifests joined extra-files on 2026-09-06 after sitting at 9.5.4 for forty releases because nothing stamped them. That fix reached the sources and stopped short of the mirrors. Same defect, one layer down. Which is why the test below matters more than the two-line config change above.

Phrasing the invariant so it does not need an allowlist

"Every versioned plugin.json must be stamped" is the obvious rule and it is wrong. It would demand stamping tests/fixtures/fn-hooks-canary/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, pinned at 0.0.1 on purpose, whose pinned version is exactly what it asserts.

Tying the rule to the drift roster gets that right for a reason: a file outside the roster can be stale without failing anything, so nothing forces it to be stamped. Fixtures fall out naturally. An allowlist would be the thing that goes stale and recreates this a fourth time.

Scope, and the draft that was too loud

draftoffenders reportedverdict
every tracked JSON with a version119switched off within a day
files named plugin.json7 scanned, 0 offenders after the fixbelievable

Most of the 119 were per-skill metadata.json and test-cases.json, whose version is the skill's own and has no relationship to the release. A plugin manifest is different: its version is what a host reads to decide what it installed.

Proven to fail, in both directions

ARM 1: drop the cursor mirror from extra-files   went red
ARM 2: stamp the canary fixture                 went red
restored                                        green, 5/5

The second arm is the one that is easy to leave out. Without it, a future edit that "helpfully" stamps the fixture would pass.

node tests/ci/test-versioned-manifests-stamped.mjs
The test reads the drift roster out of ci.yml rather than hardcoding it, so the two cannot drift apart. Hardcoding would be the same defect one level up: a test that keeps passing while guarding a roster that no longer exists.
